object_description: three separate buildings with large four-sided roofs recalling rural houses, linked by a slab
geometry_property: sectional play in the classroom building
design_condition: the programme is split into three volumes recalling the hamlet character and the large-roofed rural houses of the region, arranged on either side of a stream that is redeveloped and slightly rerouted

positive: The project refers to the hamlet character of the local constructions and the shape of the rural houses
It proposes to magnify the stream by redeveloping it and slightly modifying its route
The programme is developed in three separate buildings with clear functional assignment
The first classroom building plays skilfully with the section and offers two distinct entrances
The upper entrance leads to rooms easily accessible outside school hours
Access to the gymnasium opens directly onto a gallery serving changing rooms and stands
The jury welcomes the fact that the gymnasium is generously lit naturally
The use of wood is attractive
The jury is won over by the sensitive and respectful approach to traditions and by the presentation
negative: The extension building encroaches largely on the planned playground, contrary to the programme
An access road has to be built very close to the gymnasium
The large connecting slab as outdoor space is relatively little sunny and not very generous
The refectory and its kitchen have no natural light
The arrangement produces significant heights downstream, not respecting the dimensions imposed by the regulations
The gallery distributing the retractable stands is relatively narrow
The vertical wooden slat cladding seriously raises the question of facade maintenance
Transcribing morphological aspects so literally is questioned, as the volumes hold a different programme and size
